content: In France, the social security system ensures that prenatal and postnatal care in public hospitals is free. Working women receive 16 weeks of maternity leave with daily compensation between €9.29 and €84.90, depending on prior earnings. Financially, pregnancy and childbirth do not create additional hardship—low-income families still struggle, but no more than usual, while affluent families remain comfortable. However, new mothers receive little support beyond this. Paternity leave is just 11 days, leaving mothers to recuperate from childbirth alone while handling constant newborn care. They also face the challenge of finding childcare, as state-provided options are inadequate, particularly in Paris. Daycare costs can be as low as €1,000 annually for lower-income families, but availability is scarce, with only one spot per eight children. Many turn to private childminders or in-home care instead.
